question: What does the area under a velocity-time graph represent for motion along a straight line?

options.text: The total distance between two points
The total displacement of the object
The final velocity of the object

solution:
The correct answer is __**The total displacement of the object**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **area** under a **velocity-time (v-t) graph** for an object moving in a **straight line** represents the **total displacement** of the object during a given **time interval**.
 
• In a **velocity-time graph**, the **velocity** is plotted on the **y-axis** and **time** is plotted on the **x-axis**. Since **displacement** is defined as the product of **velocity** and **time** (s = v × t), the **geometric area** formed between the plot and the **time axis** signifies the **change in position**.
 
• Because **velocity** is a **vector quantity**, the area can be **positive** (above the time axis) or **negative** (below the time axis). The **algebraic sum** of these areas gives the **net displacement**. ***Hence, option 2 is correct.***
